claim: The Arena di Verona is the city's standout sight, a Roman amphitheatre that hosts a summer Opera Festival (12 June - 12 September 2026) with tickets from cheap unreserved stone steps up to premium numbered seats.
quote: Arena di Verona Opera Festival 2026 | 12 June - 12 September 2026

claim: Daytime sightseeing admission to the Verona Arena runs roughly EUR 10-15 adult / EUR 9 reduced, free for children under 8, open Tue-Sun 9:00-19:00 (last entry 18:30) and Mon 13:30-19:00, with early 15:00/16:00 closing on opera-performance days.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday: 9:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m. (last admission at 6:30 p.m.); Monday: 1:30 PM - 7:00 PM. On days with evening events, there is early closing at 3:00 PM or 4:00 PM

claim: Casa di Giulietta is the most debated 'tourist trap' in Verona; from 1 April 2026 entry costs EUR 5 for courtyard-only or EUR 12 for the full house and balcony, the courtyard is no longer free, and online timed reservation is mandatory even for free/VeronaCard entry.
quote: From April 1, 2026, tickets cost EUR 5 for just the courtyard and Teatro Nuovo, or EUR 12 for access to the full house and balcony. The courtyard is no longer free to enter... Online reservation for the visit is mandatory

claim: Traveller consensus on Casa di Giulietta is mixed-to-critical: it is overcrowded, staged and selfie-heavy with no real historical basis, and many advise enjoying the courtyard briefly and skipping the paid interior unless travelling as a couple or a Romeo-and-Juliet fan.
quote: if you dislike timed-entry queues, staged attractions, or very selfie-heavy spaces, you may prefer to enjoy the courtyard briefly and focus your time on Verona's churches, squares, and river viewpoints

claim: Verona's main churches (San Zeno, Duomo cathedral complex, Sant'Anastasia, San Fermo) are managed jointly by Chiese Vive; a single ticket can be bought in the first church visited, and summer hours generally run Mon-Fri ~9:30-18:30 with shorter Saturday and Sunday-afternoon hours.
quote: San Zeno: March 1 - October 31: Mon-Fri 9:00 AM-6:30 PM... You can purchase the entrance tickets in the first church you will visit.

claim: Basilica di San Zeno Maggiore charges EUR 4 single-church admission, and a combined ticket covering Verona's major churches costs EUR 6 full / EUR 5 reduced.
quote: Single Church Ticket: 4.00 EUR for adults... There is a Combi-Ticket available for all the major churches of Verona. The full price for it is 6 EUR, the reduced price is 5 EUR.

claim: San Zeno is widely rated one of the finest Romanesque churches in northern Italy, prized for its bronze doors, Andrea Mantegna triptych altarpiece, crypt and cloister, and its tufa-and-brick facade.
quote: one of the most beautiful and better preserved examples of Romanesque architecture in the whole of Northern Italy... 'Bronze Doors' and a 'Triptych A. Mantegna'

claim: Verona's Duomo (cathedral complex) is worth the stop chiefly for Titian's Assumption of the Virgin (1535), plus the octagonal single-block marble font in the Baptistery of San Giovanni in Fonte and the early-layer Church of Sant'Elena; admission is about EUR 4 covering three buildings or EUR 8 for the four-church combined ticket.
quote: Admission is EUR 4... ticket gives you access to three buildings of the complex including the Duomo, the Church of St Helen, and the Baptistry of St. John. Another option... pay EUR 8... to get access to four churches

claim: Torre dei Lamberti, the 84m medieval tower rising over Piazza delle Erbe, is the recommended panoramic viewpoint of Verona, reachable by 368 steps or a glass elevator, costing about EUR 6 adult / EUR 4.50 reduced and open daily.
quote: Tickets cost EUR 6 for adults and EUR 4.50 for students and seniors... You can reach the top via the 368 steps inside of the tower, or the glass-sided elevator

claim: Torre dei Lamberti is rated a must-see for the only true bird's-eye view of Verona's rooftops and, on clear days, the surrounding mountains, with early morning or late-afternoon/sunset the best times to climb.
quote: a must-see for visitors to the city as there's no other place like it to get a bird-eye view of Verona... best time to visit is either early morning to avoid crowds or late afternoon for stunning sunset views

claim: The Arche Scaligere, five Gothic della-Scala family tombs in a railed courtyard beside Piazza dei Signori, are a high-impact, low-time medieval stop fully visible for free through the wrought-iron fence, with courtyard entry possible in the April-September season.
quote: the monuments are visually unforgettable... an excellent 'texture stop' between bigger attractions... The Arche are also perfectly visible from the outside. The wrought iron fence allows the vision of both the sarcophagi on the ground and those on raised floors.

claim: The Arche Scaligere are officially described as one of the most important Gothic funerary complexes in Italy, monumental and richly decorated, often underestimated because they blend into the urban fabric.
quote: One of the most important Gothic funerary complexes in Italy, often underestimated because it fits into the urban fabric. The arks are monumental and richly decorated, and deserve a careful stop

claim: The VeronaCard (24h EUR 27 / 48h EUR 32) bundles fast-track Arena entry plus Casa di Giulietta, Torre dei Lamberti, Castelvecchio, San Zeno, the cathedral complex, the Scaliger Tombs and free public transport; municipal sites including the Arena and Casa di Giulietta close on Mondays.
quote: 24-hour card for EUR 27 and a 48-hour card for EUR 32... Arena Amphitheatre, Casa di Giulietta, Torre dei Lamberti, Castelvecchio Museum, Basilica di San Zeno Maggiore, Verona Cathedral complex, and Scaliger Tombs... closed on Mondays
